item: The in-memory keyword rollup build no longer holds the corpus in memory, stages 490 times faster, stops on the memory guard, and a killed build is not restarted identically
summary: Diagnostics of 2026-10-06: on eight 4.81 GiB VMs the build was killed by the kernel 12 times in 4.7 days and restarted identically after every restart (about 2,000 bytes a keyword as ORM entities in one list, 7.5 to 8.8 GB for 3.8 to 4.4 million keywords; executemany staging at 1.1 thousand rows/s). The keyword projection now streams as a column-projected keyset, and both streams go into DuckDB as JSON column arrays in one statement (563 thousand rows/s measured, no new dependency, no file written). The guard is polled after every batch; a start check compares DuckDB's limit, one batch and the guard's floor with available memory; an in-progress marker in the data dir turns a killed build into a declined one (last_build_killed) until the machine has what the dead process held; an encrypted corpus gets no DuckDB offload directory, a plaintext one a per-process folder swept at the next start. Also from the coordinator's check of PR #1305: the slow-step warning is logged while the step runs, a build thread that cannot start releases the lock, and a BaseException is not recorded as done. REVIEW FIXES AT THE FINAL HEAD (Opus read, one block, seven should-fix): the JSON staging's fallback no longer swallows DuckDB's own memory limit (an encrypted corpus that outgrew it re-ran the batch at 1.2 thousand rows/s instead of declining); a build stopped part-way is held by its own measured rule and not rescanned by the next serve request; the marker keeps the PEAK and is written when the final aggregation starts, its retry rule counts what the build GREW by (not the whole resident size, which counted the app's baseline twice) and a normal quit clears it through atexit; the guard is asked at most once a second; a refused boot-step timer thread no longer leaves a step 'running'; the spill sweep runs for an encrypted corpus too and a reused pid starts empty; the start and kill checks do not gate the persisted refresh; tests no longer depend on the host's free memory. A SECOND READ (of the fixes) FOUND AND FIXED: one offload folder PER CONNECTION (a rebuild stages beside the rollup it replaces; a shared folder failed the serving connection's queries and once killed the process), removed after that connection closes; a guard stop held on the projected total growth and any hold released when the corpus epoch changes; the exit clear takes the marker's write lock so a build thread cannot rewrite it during shutdown; the stop hold skips the persisted path.
